verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你是伸冤的　神；伸冤的　神啊，求你发出光来！
verses.en: O Lord, the God who avenges!O God who avenges, reveal your splendor.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 94. The psalmist asks God to judge the wicked and affirms his confidence in God’s justice.

verses.zh: 审判世界的主啊，求你挺身而立，使骄傲人受应得的报应！
verses.en: Rise up, O judge of the earth.Pay back the proud.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，恶人夸胜要到几时呢？要到几时呢？
verses.en: O Lord, how long will the wicked,how long will the wicked celebrate?[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “shine forth” (see Pss 50:2; 80:1).

verses.zh: 他们絮絮叨叨说傲慢的话；一切作孽的人都自己夸张。
verses.en: They spew out threats[NOTE:1] and speak defiantly;all the evildoers boast.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “exult.”
Heb “they gush forth [words].”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，他们强压你的百姓，苦害你的产业。
verses.en: O Lord, they crush your people;they oppress the nation that belongs to you.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hitpael of אָמַר (ʾamar) occurs only here (and perhaps in Isa 61:6).

verses.zh: 他们杀死寡妇和寄居的，又杀害孤儿。
verses.en: They kill the widow and the resident foreigner,and they murder the fatherless.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “your inheritance.”

verses.zh: 他们说：耶和华必不看见；雅各的　神必不思念。
verses.en: Then they say, “The Lord does not see this;the God of Jacob does not take notice of it.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew noun יָתוֹם (yatom) refers to one who has lost his father (not necessarily his mother, see Ps 109:9). Because they were so vulnerable and were frequently exploited, fatherless children are often mentioned as epitomizing the oppressed (see Pss 10:14; 68:5; 82:3; 146:9; as well as Job 6:27; 22:9; 24:3, 9; 29:12; 31:17, 21).

verses.zh: 你们民间的畜类人当思想；你们愚顽人到几时才有智慧呢？
verses.en: Take notice of this,[NOTE:1] you ignorant people.[NOTE:2] You fools, when will you ever understand?
notes: Heb “does not understand.”
Heb “understand.” The verb used in v. 7 is repeated here for rhetorical effect. The people referred to here claim God is ignorant of their actions, but the psalmist corrects their faulty viewpoint.

verses.zh: 造耳朵的，难道自己不听见吗？造眼睛的，难道自己不看见吗？
verses.en: Does the one who makes the human ear not hear?Does the one who forms the human eye not see?[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “[you] brutish among the people.”

verses.zh: 管教列邦的，就是叫人得知识的，难道自己不惩治人吗？
verses.en: Does the one who disciplines the nations not punish?He is the one who imparts knowledge to human beings!

verses.zh: 耶和华知道人的意念是虚妄的。
verses.en: The Lord knows that peoples’ thoughts are morally bankrupt.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “The one who plants an ear, does he not hear? The one who forms an eye, does he not see?”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你所管教、用律法所教训的人是有福的！
verses.en: How blessed is the one[NOTE:1] whom you instruct, O Lord,the one whom you teach from your law
notes: Heb “the Lord knows the thoughts of man, that they are emptiness.” The psalmist thinks specifically of the “thoughts” expressed in v. 7.

verses.zh: 你使他在遭难的日子得享平安；惟有恶人陷在所挖的坑中。
verses.en: in order to protect him from times of trouble,[NOTE:1] until the wicked are destroyed.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[Oh] the happiness [of] the man.” Hebrew wisdom literature often assumes and reflects the male-oriented perspective of ancient Israelite society. The principle of the psalm is certainly applicable to all people, regardless of their gender or age. To facilitate modern application, we translate the gender and age specific “man” with the more neutral “one.” The generic masculine pronoun is used in v. 2.
Heb “to give him rest from the days of trouble.”

verses.zh: 因为耶和华必不丢弃他的百姓，也不离弃他的产业。
verses.en: Certainly[NOTE:1] the Lord does not forsake his people;he does not abandon the nation that belongs to him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “until a pit is dug for the wicked.”
Or “for.”

verses.zh: 审判要转向公义；心里正直的，必都随从。
verses.en: For justice will prevail,[NOTE:1] and all the morally upright[NOTE:2] will be vindicated.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “his inheritance.”
Heb “for judgment will return to justice.”

Heb “all the pure of heart.” The “heart” is here viewed as the seat of one’s moral character and motives. The “pure of heart” are God’s faithful followers who trust in and love the Lord and, as a result, experience his deliverance (see Pss 7:10; 11:2; 32:11; 36:10; 64:10; 97:11).

verses.zh: 谁肯为我起来攻击作恶的？谁肯为我站起抵挡作孽的？
verses.en: Who will rise up to defend me[NOTE:1] against the wicked?Who will stand up for me against the evildoers?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and after it [are] the pure of heart.”
Heb “for me.”

verses.zh: 若不是耶和华帮助我，我就住在寂静之中了。
verses.en: If the Lord had not helped me,I would soon have dwelt in the silence of death.[NOTE:1]
notes: Who will stand up for me…? The questions anticipate the answer, “No one except God” (see v. 17).

verses.zh: 我正说我失了脚，耶和华啊，那时你的慈爱扶助我。
verses.en: If I say, “My foot is slipping,”your loyal love, O Lord, supports me.

verses.zh: 我心里多忧多疑，你安慰我，就使我欢乐。
verses.en: When worries threaten to overwhelm me,[NOTE:1] your soothing touch makes me happy.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “If the Lord [were] not my help, quickly my life would have dwelt in silence.” The psalmist, perhaps speaking as the nation’s representative, recalls God’s past intervention. For other examples of conditional sentences with the term לוּלֵי (lule, “if not”) in the protasis and a perfect verbal form in the apodosis, see Pss 119:92 and 124:2-5.
Heb “when my worries are many within me.”

verses.zh: 那藉着律例架弄残害、在位上行奸恶的，岂能与你相交吗？
verses.en: Cruel rulers[NOTE:1] are not your allies,those who make oppressive laws.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “your comforts cause my soul to delight.”
Heb “a throne of destruction.” “Throne” stands here by metonymy for rulers who occupy thrones.

verses.zh: 他们大家聚集攻击义人，将无辜的人定为死罪。
verses.en: They conspire against[NOTE:1] the blameless[NOTE:2] and condemn to death the innocent.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Is a throne of destruction united to you, one that forms trouble upon a statute?” The rhetorical question anticipates the answer, “Of course not!” The translation, while not preserving the interrogative form of the statement, reflects its rhetorical force.
Or “attack.”
Heb “the life of the blameless.”

verses.zh: 但耶和华向来作了我的高台；我的　神作了我投靠的磐石。
verses.en: But the Lord will protect me,[NOTE:1] and my God will shelter me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and the blood of the innocent they declare guilty.”
Heb “and the Lord has become my elevated place.” The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) consecutive is used in a rhetorical sense, describing an anticipated development as if it were already reality.

verses.zh: 他叫他们的罪孽归到他们身上。他们正在行恶之中，他要剪除他们；耶和华―我们的　神要把他们剪除。
verses.en: He will pay them back for their sin.[NOTE:1] He will destroy them because of[NOTE:2] their evil;the Lord our God will destroy them.
notes: Heb “and my God [has become] a rocky summit of my safety.”
The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) consecutive is used in a rhetorical sense, describing an anticipated development as if it were already reality.
